**Why the model flagged a high risk**  
The model looks at three key pieces of information it has about you. First, your revolving‑credit utilization is essentially 100 % (0.9999999). Using almost all of the credit you have available is a strong signal that you may have difficulty meeting future payments, and it pushes the default risk upward. Second, your age of 30 years also adds a modest amount of risk in the model’s view. Finally, you have only one open credit line or loan; having more open accounts would have lowered the risk a little, so this factor works in your favor but not enough to offset the other two.

**How you can improve the decision**  
The model shows a clear path to a much lower risk score: bring your revolving‑credit utilization down to 0 by paying off the balances on your credit cards or other revolving accounts. Reducing utilization from near‑full to zero is expected to drop the predicted default probability from about 61 % to roughly 16 %, moving you into a much safer range for credit approval.
